operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: roller_coaster 6 rows, country 3 rows; no sampling cap needed, original_values are complete.
Mixed-case identifiers: "Roller_Coaster_ID", "Name", "Country_ID" — must be double-quoted; column lookup case-insensitive.
DDL uses backtick-quoted parent `country`("Country_ID") in FK clause — sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim for the clone.
FK roller_coaster.Country_ID -> country.Country_ID, parent exists, parent is PK (unique) — clean FK, no dangling.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints anywhere; only PKs. Insert failures will be rare (PK dupes only).
Speed is declared TEXT but stores numeric-looking strings ('51','55','37.9') — String fuzzer, not Number.
Opened is declared TEXT storing mixed date formats: 'August 31, 2007', 'May 14, 2005' (month-name) and bare years '2012','2011'.
Status has distinct=1 ('Operating') — String sampler with one element; contaminate will still mutate it.
Length/Height REAL with integer-valued samples (3236.0) — Number float path, +-0.01 perturbation.
Country_ID in roller_coaster has distinct=3 < 6 rows — FK column will have ties/duplicates by construction.
Park contains non-ASCII 'Gröna Lund' — String CHARSET is ASCII-only, so fresh draws lose the umlaut (fine, but note).
No views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs; clone is just two CREATE TABLEs.
operator_ts_expectations: Opened: declared TEXT -> String fuzzer (not Date), so TS emits random a-zA-Z0-9() strings, never date-shaped — kills any date-format query.
Speed: String fuzzer over numeric strings; int-like elements get +-1 neighbors, so '51'->'50'/'52' plausible, but fresh draws are gibberish.
Status: single element 'Operating' with p=0.2 fresh draws -> mostly 'Operating' plus contaminated variants; equality filters on 'Operating' often still match.
Country_ID FK: child draws from parent's final Country_ID values with replacement -> heavy ties, so joins produce duplicate rows; GROUP BY/COUNT DISTINCT queries may still pass.
Roller_Coaster_ID PK: single-column PK -> max_l0=inf, fresh Number draws in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from INT (scale=0) -> small ints, collisions dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys.
Length/Height: Number float, list range quirk (upper end overwritten to full range) -> values can be far outside [1574,4726] / [50,136], implausible lengths/heights.
Population/Area: Number int, full range [-1,1] for scale=0 -> mostly -1/0/1, wildly implausible vs 5-9M populations; drives FN on range predicates.
Name/Park/Languages: String length range from elements (e.g. [3,20]) -> random ASCII strings, no real country/park names; equality on 'Austria' etc. fails unless element drawn.
Tiny tables (3-6 rows) mean choose_table_sizes level-0 = 1+30u -> up to ~31 rows, so TS inflates country to ~30 rows with random names — plausible FP source for COUNT(*) queries.
No Date fuzzer anywhere (no 'date'/'timestamp' declared type) — date-format misses are structural, not fuzzer-template.
FK consistency: child Country_ID always in parent's final set, so referential-integrity queries (anti-join for orphans) return empty — FN for 'find orphan' golds.
